243	*History, kept so the acceptance rows read.* Before the ruling, a player with the cell spent, zero sticks and an unlit console was in a true soft-lock and it was the expected end of a long lit session (D.10: about 4 survey sorties spend the cell), with the dock survivable (`a_dock` `T0` -6000 mC) so that no death and no restore ever fired; Interaction had refused the lit exemption, Web Map had declined the stronger lint, and the loose-glowstick fallback was unsound (a loose stick is unlit until thrown and `pickup` is lit-only). The existing mitigations (the two-stick `a_dock` shelf, `ls_a_dock_shelf`; the four-stick home airlock supply, `ls_air_locker`, DA-26; drop, throw, re-take, IA-29) still narrow the dark-drop case and are no longer load-bearing for the hop. **The invariant is BLOCKING for the implementation of this system** (stage-12 ruling after the CD-GDD-ALIGN concern: P5 says failure costs ship and body and never a soft-lock): the sortie is not implementation-complete, and the slice does not ship, while AC-BS-92 (a bounded reachability test over the matrix and the campaign-length strand cell) or AC-BS-51b (the placement lint and the console-in-glow check) is red; no sign-off replaces them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
244	
245	*Mechanisms considered (history of the ruling).* **M1**, a console-only lit exemption in IA-6, was refused by Interaction and is not taken. **M3**, a reserved lamp charge only the console press can spend, was not taken. **M2**, a pod-owned console lamp, is the nearest: the ruled mechanism is a self-powered status glow on the docked pod's prop, an ordinary fixture and not a lamp off the derelict bus. Rejected throughout: allowing `throw_glowstick` while carrying (it removes the BS-5 cost of lighting the drop zone first). *Pillar.* P5, P2. *Decided.* run ruling R3 (level-designer LD-R6); the stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN revision made the invariant binding; the user ruled the mechanism and the cell policy on 2026-10-27 (OQ-BS-4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
246	
247	**BS-20 — Content-side sortie constraints are citations; one design target.** *Rule.* These Derelict Authoring bounds are lint-backed facts Boarding relies on and re-checks across **all five loaded sets** S0 to S4 and both sortie orders (never only the first sortie): a carried round trip to the farthest salvage through an unbreathable stretch inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; a hazard crossing of at most 7 tiles of lethal cold (5.6 s); `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 1800, 600 when carrying (the endogenous-fault escape bound, DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound); 18 / 22 module nodes (A / B); four loose parts *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the loose ledger (DA-28, DA-29, DA-21, DA-25, DA-26, DA-32). **Design target, not a lint and not registered:** a first sortie to A completes cut and carry-home in about five minutes of *player time* (concept Core Loop; measured as W_LOOP, home console press to install, with its median W_ABOARD part kept below Sanity's stage-1 point, D.1 and D.8; a long sortie that enters stage 1 is intended: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D73 part (c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with `RESERVE_S` [PLACEHOLDER] and `CELL_S` [PLACEHOLDER] sufficient. The route itself is a minute-scale lower bound; the five minutes are listening, lighting, deciding and door choices, so nobody tunes the route up to hit five minutes by distance (`V_CARRY` is locked). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D73): the concept's five-minute W_LOOP is kept and content is budgeted for about 200 s of discretionary dwell (D.1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One target:** W_LOOP (home console press to install) is the single five-minute target and every other figure derives from it: the W_ABOARD target is W_LOOP less the non-interactive pod legs and the home leg, about 259 s at the defaults (Tuning Knobs, Design targets), and the 300 s figure of D.8 and the 5-minute top of the X-BS-1 band are the stage-1 ceiling on the median, not second targets. The ruled decision carry of about 21 to 28 tiles (X3) lies with at most 7 tiles (336 px) of it inside `a_machine` (the lethal-cold cap, DA-28; DA-48 measures the carry from the cut point and its proposal puts 228 px there) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; whether a 1008 to 1344 px carried leg passes `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 600 when carrying (DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound) is Derelict Authoring's lint question (OQ-BS-31). This GDD's reading: the 600 px bound is the endogenous-fault escape bound and does not apply to a non-fault decision carry; if Derelict Authoring's lint applies it to every carried leg, the ruled decision carry needs an explicit exemption, or the lint rejects the ruled route (ASK-BS-D4 (e), AC-BS-52) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Sanity's dwell cost is cited and not set: `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` [PLACEHOLDER] (SN). **Subject budget:** Boarding adds no subject beyond the drops `P <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` and forbids any rule here that seeds more loose items; the post-weld sortie S4 `{home+B, A}` already exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 24 (144 vs 120, DA OQ-DA-20, owned by Derelict Authoring and Interaction, C-BS-7). Node anchors are not published by Derelict Authoring, so every route figure in this GDD is marked as assumed and deferred to Layout's `route_length_px` (ASK-BS-D1). *Why.* The authored bounds are what keep a carried return survivable and a retreat legal across every loaded set; citing them and minting no lint of Boarding's own keeps Derelict Authoring the one owner of the geometry, while the design target names only the felt length. *Pillar.* P2, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R23, R24, R29.
248	
249	**BS-21 — Autosave after a cut.** *Rule.* "Section extraction" in SL-4 is **Assembly's detach** (BDY:341) and is already served by MSA-33's derived read `last_shape_change_T()`, polled by Save/Load; Boarding neither owns nor names it. For a **module** cut, a completed V8 should also shorten the loss window, following the same pattern: Interaction publishes a pure derived read of the last salvage-completion tick (the read `last_salvage_T()` (registry: `last_salvage_T`); **Boarding mints no name**, which is this GDD's answer to Save/Load OQ-24), Save/Load polls it under SL-5's gate and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, and `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` guards a doomed save (SL-4, SL-5, SL-7, SL-8). A tell defers through SL-5 soft row (b) (provisional; an absent Attention view counts as open and logs `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT`); a channel, stagger or transit defers through `GATE_SOFT_STATES`; DOWNED and DEAD are hard. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **User rulings X7, D14, D42, D17:** (a) any bound seat whose `vitals_state` is CRITICAL or worse is a third soft-gate input (a due save is deferred up to the cap, then written `RISKY`, with no glyph), also applied to `quit_risky`; (b) the fairness step-back: a death restore also steps back one generation when `T_downed - g_r.T` is under `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` (600 ticks); (c) a post-DOWNED refractory of `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` ticks. The module-cut event autosave, with the weld and seam-cut events, is **confirmed** (D17; the escape hatch is a data change and metric M5). Assembly's seam-cut event autosave is withheld while the self-inflicted RAGGED decompression runs (until the keep-side cut room has vented and its ports are capped or past the port ceiling, D54, MSA-33) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and does not apply to a module cut, whose SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window; the fault loss window (mean about 5400, max 10,800, ceiling 18,000 ticks, D55) is Assembly's and Save/Load's. The ruled text is Save/Load's (SL-5, SL-8); D.9 prints the gate list. `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state, so an autosave may land mid-carry; a cut's SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window. The read therefore cannot trap the player in a doomed state. The brief's push-event idea is not adopted (Boarding cannot emit one, BS-1). *Why.* The loss ceiling (340 s, 5.7 minutes: SL's `loss_max` of 20,400 ticks, D.9) is longer than a whole five-minute sortie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Pillar.* P5 (loss is not total). *Decided.* run ruling R6; ASK-BS-I4, ASK-BS-L1.
250	
251	**BS-22 — Art direction owned here: severed stubs, the cap piece, and one shared carried-module sprite.** *Rule.* Boarding owns the **art direction and states** of the severed-stub pieces (kit gap K-9; DA:526, DA:1341, DA:1465) for `/asset-spec`: one STUB per open fluid port; hissing until capped (the sound is Audio's); a cap piece after `begin_cap`; the pedestal rect stays (LY-20) and the scorched kerf is Interaction's V8 completion row; all **hue-less, matte, mechanical, no glow, no body vocabulary in any sprite, palette or sound brief** (ART 4.4; the flesh and violet palette is reserved for sanity leaks). All carried modules, real or (VS-A) phantom, draw as **one plain shape drawn once on the tool layer** (ART:512, ART:815), so a real and a phantom carry look alike; identity is known from the loose sprite at pickup and from the body cue, not from the carried sprite (closes IA Open Question 23). The carry frames keep the chest point and the forward beam arc unobstructed (ART:1221); pose is **ruled by the art-director: the module is held overhead**, centred over the helmet with its bottom edge at least 2 px above the crown, the sprite capped at 24 x 14 px so figure plus module is at most 71 px, under the 72 px wall front face (ART 8.2; AD-BS-1, AD-BS-2; C-BS-5 closed). The PC-8 phrase "below the lamp" is refreshed (refresh row 19). *Why.* A hue-less, matte stub stays on the truth side of the sane palette, and one shared carried sprite means a real and a phantom carry can be told apart only by the body cue and the checks, never by the drawing. *Pillar.* P1, P4 (parity). *Decided.* run rulings R21, R22.
252	
253	**BS-23 — Loose items and the sortie: what Boarding repeats.** *Rule.* Placement data is Derelict Authoring's ledger (DA-26), slots are Layout's (LY-22), the mechanism and holder are Interaction's (IA-28); Boarding adds only the sortie-level rules stated in BS-13 (abandon persists), BS-5 (dark drop needs light), BS-16 (the haul is finite). A module dropped then left on a section that is later welded or cut off moves with the section (items are section-local, LY-22). Wording refreshes owed to neighbours that say otherwise are listed in Cross-References and never edited here. *Why.* Restating loose-item ownership here would give one fact two writers; naming only the sortie-level consequences (abandon persists, a dark drop needs light, the haul is finite) keeps one owner per fact. *Pillar.* P5. *Decided.* run ruling R20.
254	
255	**BS-24 — What Boarding refuses (the anti-pillar rule).** *Rule.* The following do not exist in the sortie, and a rule anywhere in this GDD that implies one is a defect:
256	
257	| Refusal | Guard | Pillar or anti-pillar |
258	|---|---|---|
259	| Combat: no weapon on any def, no damage verb, no kill; the cutter cuts machines, never creatures | G-1 | not a combat game |
260	| Progression: nothing levels, unlocks or scores from salvage; the only progression is the ship's body and what the player learns (the knowledge persistence the failure contract depends on is not a progression this guard forbids) | G-2 | P5 / not a combat game |
261	| Construction: modules are pre-shaped; a take is an extraction and not a relocation; no `remove_module` | G-3 | not a freeform builder |
262	| Economy: no shop, currency, recipe, vendor, refill, loot table, rarity; salvage-once | G-4 | P5 |
263	| Readouts: no inventory screen, pack capacity, encumbrance meter, weight, value, condition or capacity number, pod scale | G-5 | P1 |
264	| Timers and meters: no sortie timer, no Attention meter (visual or audio), no `listen` verb | G-6 | P3 |
265	| Forced script: sortie order is a recommendation (DA-2); no forced drop, cap, required module or quest item; no payoff-less carry taught as the reference cut | G-7 | no authored story; P1 |
266	| PvP: no stealing from a crewmate's hands and no reward for harm (VS-B); the carry cost is the crew's shared cost; the only harm to a crewmate is the system-gated friendly-harm act, admitted only while the attacker's sanity is system-verified below the harm threshold (Sanity; IA-31), with a victim-visible tell and attribution to the web, so a sane player has no attack (P4(c)) | G-8 | no intentional PvP; P4(c) |
267	| Body metaphor in the senses: graft, severed, bleed are design prose only | G-9 | P1 sane palette |
268	| A win state in a haul: no "complete the ship", no collection checklist | G-10 | no win state |
269	| A price that lies (BS-15) | G-11 | P4 |
270	
271	Restraint and retreat are legal strategies with stated costs (BS-13). *Pillar.* the anti-pillars. *Decided.* run ruling R31; creative-director guard rails G-1 to G-11.

273	### States and Transitions
274	
275	**Boarding & Salvage has no stored state** (BS-1). The template requires a state table, so the table below is a **fixture and design vocabulary**: each label is a predicate over fields the owners already hold, computed and never written, never registered, never persisted, and never a name in any file, command or event. It exists so that the headless reference sortie (Acceptance Criteria) and the Game Feel arc can name "where in the sortie" without minting state. *(orchestrator ruling: the stage ruling R12 says "no Boarding state names"; the task requires this table; the resolution is to keep the table as test-fixture vocabulary, state this once, and let the labels be dropped or renamed at the checkpoint without touching any rule. Logged as a question.)*
276	
277	**The four owner axes the labels read** (nothing else is consulted):
278	
279	| Axis | Owner field | Values used |
280	|---|---|---|
281	| Where | `body_of_actor` / `actor_section` (BDY); `transit_state` (WM) | home body; derelict locus body; in transit (`IDLE`, `LEG`, `ARRIVING`, `BERTHING`) |
282	| What the hands do | `controller.state.loco_state` (PC) and `channel_ref` | `IDLE`, `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `IN_POD` |
283	| What is held | `controller.state.carry_ref` (PC-8), cross-checked with `suit.state.carried_id` (SE-13) | none / one carried instance |
284	| What the web is doing | Attention `phase` (AT) | `CALM`, `TELL`, `BREACH`, `SUBSIDING` |
285	
286	**Labels (derived, never stored):**
287	
288	| Label | Derived from | Entry | Exit | Legal transitions | Who may cause them |
289	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
290	| HOME | actor in the home body; `transit_state` `IDLE` | boot, or arrival from a hop | `pod_hop` Applied | to TRANSIT_OUT | the player (`pod_hop`, WM-8) |
291	| TRANSIT_OUT | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin home; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied (a body transfer; aborts any channel, IA-40) | `pod_arrive` / `pod_settle` after `HOP_LEG_TICKS` and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` | to ABOARD_QUIET | Web Map's machine (WM-14); the player only by pressing the console |
292	| ABOARD_QUIET | actor in a derelict locus body; no `channel_ref`; hands free or a tool in hand; `phase` not `TELL`/`BREACH` | arrival; a channel ends or aborts; `drop` | a channel begins; `pickup`; a TELL opens | to ABOARD_JOB, LOADED, ABOARD_TELL | the player (verbs); Attention (phase) |
293	| ABOARD_JOB | `loco_state` `CHANNELLING` on `begin_cut`, `begin_cap` or `field_check` | channel `Applied` (lit, in reach) | completion; abort (IA-15: MOVED, CANCELLED, UNLIT, OUT_OF_REACH, TARGET_GONE, BODY, NOT_ELIGIBLE, RESTORE); a TELL opens (the channel is not aborted by it) | to ABOARD_QUIET, ABOARD_TELL | the player; the abort set; Attention (phase) |
294	| LOADED | `carry_ref` set; `loco_state` `CARRY_WALK` or `IDLE` | `pickup` Applied (IA-28) | `drop`; downed (PC-9); `install_module`; `pod_hop` carries it across (state persists) | to ABOARD_QUIET (drop), HOME (via hop), INSTALLED | the player; Suit's limiter via PC-9 (downed) |
295	| ABOARD_TELL | `phase` `TELL` and the actor in the locus body | Attention enters TELL (AT-8) | abort by stillness (AT-10), breach due, or departure | to ABOARD_QUIET (abort), ABOARD_BREACH, TRANSIT_BACK | Attention only; the player's restraint or departure shapes it |
296	| ABOARD_BREACH | `phase` `BREACH` or `SUBSIDING`, actor in `locus_body` (AT-15) | tell expiry | the last recorded occupant leaves a non-home locus body (AT-22) | to TRANSIT_BACK | Attention (the harm), the player (departure) |
297	| TRANSIT_BACK | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin a derelict; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied from a dock room (always allowed, WM-26) | arrival at home | to HOME (and still LOADED if `carry_ref` is set) | the player; Web Map's machine |
298	| INSTALLED | M5 `install_module` Applied (MSA-26) | the module seated in a hardpoint | **terminal for that module** (no `remove_module`, MSA-28; V8 salvage is the only way out) | none | the player (`install_module`) |
299	| DOWNED | `loco_state` `DOWNED` (Suit limiter FAILED, SE-24) | the limiter reaches FAILED | revive (VS-B); the solo give-up-and-reload action (user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` elapses, then DEAD, then restore from the newest autosave (SL-7) | to ABOARD_QUIET (revive), restore | Suit/Controller (the limiter); the host (restore) |
300	
301	**Transition rules worth stating once.**
302	
303	1. **LOADED is an overlay, not a place.** It combines with every aboard label (a tell during a carry is ABOARD_TELL and LOADED at once); the fixture reports both.
304	2. **Any aboard label may go to TRANSIT_BACK from any dock room with the pod docked there, whatever the cargo** (WM-26, WM:414 envelope). If the console row is refused (C-BS-1), a LOADED actor must first `drop` and the module stays aboard (Edge Cases).
305	3. **A tell does not interrupt a hop, and a hop does not interrupt a tell** (AT-22, WM-26), but a hop that leaves a derelict locus voids the due-run breach if every seat recorded at tell entry has left by then (AT-22; user ruling D46 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); a departed derelict goes dormant and its state stands still (WM-24, LS-17).
306	4. **Restore returns each axis to its owner's snapshot** and the labels are recomputed: `CHANNELLING` and `STAGGERED` go to `IDLE`, `carry_ref` is restored with the Suit's instance and cross-checked (PC-17, SE-13 `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`); Interaction's `post_restore` never touches `carry_ref` (IA-28); a cut that completed before the autosave stands, one that did not is as if never begun (the ledger is Interaction's).
307	5. **Nothing here is guarded by Boarding.** Every transition is caused by a verb, a hop or an Attention phase that an owner validates; Boarding adds no guard, no timeout and no side effect to any of them.
308	
309	*Why.* A named, registered sortie machine would restate `loco_state`, the Attention phase and `transit_state` (run ruling R12). *Pillar.* P3 (the cost is in the steps, not in a state). *Decided.* run ruling R12 (the table kept as fixture vocabulary).

311	### Interactions with Other Systems
312	
313	Boarding & Salvage owns **no interface** (BS-1): no hook, no mutator, no read view, no command, no notification, no dirty key. "Data in" below is what the sortie reads from an owner; "data out" is what the sortie supplies — which is always a rule, a content constraint, a procedure or a routed ask, never runtime data. Every name in the interface column is fixed by its owner (the kernel, the Graph, the Controller, Interaction, Suit, Assembly, Sanity, Web Map, Save/Load); where an owner has not fixed it, the cell says so. **Each row quotes the neighbour's own counterpart row so bidirectionality can be checked line by line.** Status: **Designed** unless marked *provisional*.
314	
315	#### A. The five index dependencies (Dependency Map position 11)
316	
317	| System | Data in to the sortie | Data out (Boarding supplies) | Interface owner and fixed names | Counterpart row, quoted |
318	|---|---|---|---|---|

361	## Formulas

363	**Scope and conventions (read first; every formula below uses them).** Every formula here is **design-time: not hashed, not persisted and never read by the simulation** (Boarding registers no state and no constant, BS-1, R1; the SN:529 precedent). Each is an analysis that the designers and the headless reference sortie can recompute, and each leans on an owner's formula **by name and never restates it**: `attention_integrator` (Attention), `held_mass_cue` (Suit), IDB F-13 `haul_cost` and F-15 `patch_launder` (`T_cycle`), SN D.7 (check cost), DA D.10 `cold_room_exposure`, WM D.4 `hop_fuel`, SL `loss_ticks`. Arithmetic is integer: `ceil` and `floor` act on non-negative operands, shares are in permille, and every Attention result is the **discrete, run-quantised integer** of the integrator (the level `L` and baseline `B` in mAU, 1 AU = 1000 mAU = one walking tick of noise, six ticks per run), recomputed from `attention_integrator` with the light and power terms zeroed unless a row says otherwise; the closed-form `ln` and `e^` estimates of the specialist drafts are used only as labelled cross-checks. Three caveats apply to every number. (1) Every sortie time is a **lower bound** while the tool-swap duration is unregistered (`T_EQUIP`, SN OQ-SN-6, carried as 0), and `pickup` and `drop` are TAPs with no registered duration (carried as 0). (2) Every Attention result depends on the [PLACEHOLDER] values of `U_TOOL`, `U_LOUD`, `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, `ATT_THRESHOLD`, `HOLD_PM` [PLACEHOLDER], `B_table`, `TELL_DRAW_LO` [PLACEHOLDER] and `TELL_DRAW_HI` [PLACEHOLDER]. (3) Every route figure rests on **assumed node anchors**: Derelict Authoring publishes room rects, door spans and the `arrive_*` cells but no node anchors, so legs are Manhattan distances from door centres to an anchor tagged `[ASSUMED anchor]`, and Layout's `route_length_px` governs once published (DA-29, ASK-BS-D1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Four more caveats follow from the rulings. (4) The carry burden `U_BURDEN` 7 [PLACEHOLDER] is Attention's registered value and its recalibration is run (F-26): the D.2 figures that use them quote Attention's integrator with the decay suspended while salvage is held (delegated ruling R5), and D.2 uses Attention's fixed 312-tick golden walk-in where D.1 scales the walk-in with the route *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. (5) The pod glow's light term is Emitter State's `[PLACEHOLDER]`: the lit figures printed below are snapshots without it, and `REF_GOLDEN` is regenerated with it. (6) The 13-tile `htr_a` leg is the pre-ruling authored anchor; the ruled decision route is 21 to 28 tiles (Derelict Authoring places it) and both are printed. (7) Derivations of this amendment were run with the same integer recursion that reproduces the golden figures (1,756,600 mAU noise-only peak; 3,394,795 mAU lit peak) exactly. *Orchestrator ruling: the specialist drafts disagreed on three inputs; this GDD adopts the checkpoint's `TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 for the played tell (K1), Sanity's run of 12 ticks, 5 per second, for dwell (SN conventions; the primary draft assumed 10 per second), and the registry's per-step leak column of IDB-7 as already-halved (the primary draft applied `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` twice).*

586	### D.6 `modules_per_fuel`
587	
588	The modules_per_fuel formula is defined as:
589	
590	`hop_ok(pool) <=> pool - HOP_FUEL_ML >= HOP_FUEL_FLOOR_ML` (a hop from HOME; WM D.4) ; `hops_max(t) = max(0, floor((F0 - burn(t) - HOP_FUEL_FLOOR_ML) / HOP_FUEL_ML))` ; `burn(t) = floor(P_W * FUEL_UML_PER_W * 600 * t_min / 1,000,000)` mL ; `modules_max = hops_max` at one carried module per seat per hop (BS-12)
591	
592	**Variables:**
593	
594	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
595	|---|---|---|---|---|
596	| `F0` | int mL | 20,000 at wake (`ft_main`) | WM D.4 (the Graph's FUEL_TANK `stock_ml`) | the home pool; no MVP refuel source (WM-20) |
597	| `HOP_FUEL_ML` | int mL | 400 (100 to 2000) [PLACEHOLDER] | Web Map WM-20 | debited on departure from HOME only; the return is prepaid (`RETURN_HOP_FUEL_ML` kept 0) |
598	| `HOP_FUEL_FLOOR_ML` | int mL | 1500 (1440 to 4000) [PLACEHOLDER] | Web Map WM D.5 | the pool that must remain after the debit |
599	| `P_W` | int W | 0 to 2500 | the Graph (home draw) | the reactor's load |
600	| `FUEL_UML_PER_W` | int | 120 (40 to 400) | Graph Tuning Knobs, not a registry entry (LSG:958) | burn per watt per step |
601	| `t_min` | int min | 0 to about 100 | the session | elapsed campaign time |
602	
603	**Output Range:** `hops_max` 0 to 46 (no burn); a `berth` is a separate `BERTH_FUEL_ML` 800 [PLACEHOLDER] debit (WM-21).
604	
605	**Example:** no burn: `floor((20000 - 1500) / 400)` = **46**; the 46th hop is accepted at pool 2000 (`2000 - 400 >= 1500`), the 47th refused `FUEL_LOW` at 1600. With the reactor at full draw (2500 W, 180 mL per minute, WM D.5): after 30 min `floor((20000 - 5400 - 1500) / 400)` = 32; after 60 min 19; after 90 min 5; after 100 min 1; the last hop is accepted at a burn of 18,100 mL, about 100.56 min. One hop debits 400 mL = 2 percent of the tank = 2.2 minutes of full-draw burn. **Finding (retracts the part-1 claim, C-BS-14):** fuel is a campaign clock shared with the reactor and bounds the late campaign; it does not bound a sortie, and it is not the cap on a haul. Three useful modules from A cost three hops, 1200 mL, 6 percent of the tank. The pressure on a haul is the one carried instance, the slow walk and the tell. The MVP end-to-end script (home to A, home to B, berth B, weld, A again) debits 400, 0, 400, 0, 800, 400 = 2000 mL, 10 percent of the tank (WM D.4). *All values [PLACEHOLDER] (Web Map); revisit at the kill/continue playtest.*

The orderings: design target 300 s <= stage-1 315.8 s (nests, with 15.8 s of slack) and stage-1 315.8 s < Web Map's safe sortie 480 s < `CELL_S` 1200 s. The fuel floor therefore tolerates a longer sortie than the sanity budget does; that is acceptable (the world shows the sanity cost, not a timer) and is recorded as C-BS-12 for Web Map and Sanity. The autosave loss ceiling (340 s, 5.7 min: SL's `loss_max` 20,400 ticks, D.9) is a different axis *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Second sortie.** The nest above holds for a first sortie from `SAN_MAX`. After a 300 s W_ABOARD the level is 100,000 - 28,500 = 71,500 mSU, 1,500 above stage 1; a player who goes straight back out reaches stage 1 after `ceil(1500 / 19) / 5` = 79 / 5 = **15.8 s**. If the pod leg and the home walk and carry (about 1,431 ticks, 119 runs) count as settled, `119 * 12` = 1,428 mSU come back, `L_start(2)` is 72,928 and stage 1 arrives after `ceil(2928 / 19) / 5` = 155 / 5 = **31.0 s**. Restoring the full first-sortie envelope takes `28,500 / 12` = 2,375 settled runs = 28,500 ticks = **475 s (7.9 min)** at home. So the envelopes nest for a first sortie and for a sortie after about 8 minutes at home, and not for a second sortie in a row; this is a pacing finding for Sanity and Web Map (C-BS-12), not a Boarding rule, and it is routed, not repaired. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* A long sortie that crosses 315.8 s enters stage 1, and that is **intended** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D73 part (c); the earlier band assumed it was not): stage 1 is a priced consequence of dwelling, and the median first sortie still nests below it. *Not hashed.*
648	
649	### D.9 `loss_window_after_cut`
650	
651	The loss_window_after_cut formula is defined as:
652	
653	`t_eligible = max(t_cut_done, t_last_gen + AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS)` ; `t_save = first AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS poll at or after t_eligible with the SL-5 gate open, never later than t_eligible + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` ; `lost_cut_window = t_save - t_cut_done` ; baseline without the read: `lost_cut_window_interval = t_next_interval - t_cut_done (+ defer)` ; death side (SL, cited): `loss_max = AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS + R_g + DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` with `R_g` = 600 (the refractory-rounded warning window) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
654	
655	**Variables:**
656	
657	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
658	|---|---|---|---|---|
659	| `t_cut_done` | tick | the tick of the V8 completion | Interaction (`last_salvage_T()`, ASK-BS-I4 answered) | when the cut finished |
660	| `t_last_gen` | tick | the last generation's `T` | Save/Load | when the world was last saved |
661	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800 | registry (Save/Load) | the minimum gap between interval or event generations |
662	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` | int ticks | 10,800 | registry | the interval trigger |
663	| `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` | int ticks | 7200 | registry | the longest a soft gate defers before a `RISKY` write |
664	| `AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` | int ticks | 300 | Save/Load SL-5 | the gate re-evaluation period |
665	| `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800 | registry | the downed time before death |
666	| gate states | set | hard: DOWNED, DEAD. Soft: row (a) endogenous Graph tell (EXOGENOUS cut descriptors open none); row (b) Attention tell with fewer than `W_MIN_WARNING_S * TICK_RATE` = 600 ticks left (FAIR mode, provisional); `GATE_SOFT_STATES` CHANNELLING, STAGGERED, IN_POD; row (c) any bound seat's `vitals_state` at CRITICAL or worse (user ruling X7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); the death restore also steps back one generation when `T_downed - g_r.T < W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE`, and a post-DOWNED refractory of 600 ticks applies | Save/Load SL-5, SL-8 | what defers a due save; `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state |
667	
668	**Output Range:** with the read, `lost_cut_window` is 0 to `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` plus a gate deferral of at most `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` (0 to 9000 ticks, 1800 + 7200); without it, up to `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` = 18,000 ticks (5 min) before the next interval generation, inside SL's death-side ceiling `loss_max` = **20,400 ticks (5.7 min)**. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
669	
670	**Example:** the last generation was written at tick 7600 and the cut completes at 10,000: age 2400 is over the 1800 gap, so the cut is eligible at once; the player is IDLE or `CARRY_WALK`, neither a gate state, so it is written at the next 300-tick poll (window at most 300 ticks, 5 s) and a death on the carry restores to *after the cut*. A cut that completes 600 ticks after a generation waits 1200 ticks (20 s) for the gap; if the player is capping (CHANNELLING) or a tell has under 600 ticks left, it defers further. A save deferred 7200 ticks is written `RISKY`, and a death within `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` 3600 of restoring a `RISKY` generation steps back one generation (SL-8), so a doomed save cannot trap the player. Without the read, a cut 10 s after a generation waits for the interval generation 10,200 ticks (170 s) later, plus any gate deferral (at most `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200 ticks, 120 s; 18,000 ticks, 300 s, in total at the worst). A whole 5-minute sortie therefore fits inside one worst-case loss. *Design-time.*
671	
672	### D.10 `lamp_cell_budget`
673	
674	The lamp_cell_budget formula is defined as:
675	
676	`cell_share_pm = min(1000, floor(1000 * lit_ticks / (CELL_S * TICK_RATE)))` ; `sorties_per_cell = floor(CELL_S * TICK_RATE / lit_ticks)` for `lit_ticks >= 1`, and the sentinel `UNBOUNDED` for `lit_ticks = 0` (a dark sortie spends no cell, so the quotient does not exist) ; `sorties_to_empty = ceil(CELL_S * TICK_RATE / lit_ticks)` at a constant lit cost per sortie and no refill between sorties (the sortie in which the cell reaches 0) ; with the ruled `top_up`: `cell_after_refill = min(CELL_S * TICK_RATE, cell_left + refill_ticks)`, where `refill_ticks` is the credit of one lit bare-hand TAP at a home BATTERY port, never more than the deficit (Suit D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(the `lit_ticks = 0` guard and the clamp are the review's; `sorties_to_strand` is renamed `sorties_to_empty` because an empty cell no longer strands, BS-19; the refill term is Suit's, cited and not defined here)*
677	
678	**Variables:**
679	
680	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
681	|---|---|---|---|---|
682	| `lit_ticks` | int ticks | 0 to `T_SORTIE_SAFE_TICKS` 28,800 for a safe sortie (a lit sortie may run longer; the clamp covers it); realistic play 1,278 (the reference line) to 18,000 (a 300 s survey) | the player's beam use (`toggle_beam`, SE-8 to SE-10) | ticks with the chest lamp on while aboard and, because the statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60), ticks with the lamp left on during a hop, counted as 6 ticks per lit run (the statuses run in the pod, D60, R6): a nominal 945-tick leg holds 157 or 158 runs, so a fully lit leg debits 942 (N_lo) to 948 (N_hi) lit ticks, up to 978 on the 975-tick slack leg (163 runs); Suit drains GRAPH_STEP_TICKS per lit run (SE-8), Web Map WM-17 conforms *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
683	| `CELL_S` | int s | 1200 (600 to 2400) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | seconds of lit beam in a full cell; 72,000 ticks at the default |
684	| `RESERVE_S` | int s | 90 (45 to 240) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | engaged reserve breath, spent in an unbreathable stretch AND in the pod (the pod cabin is ANOXIC, Suit D.1 pod derivation), 47,100 to 47,400 mGU per nominal leg (D.4) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
685	| `GLOWSTICK_START_COUNT` | int | 2 (0 to 4) [PLACEHOLDER] | Suit | sticks in the start kit; each lights 150 s (`GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` [PLACEHOLDER]) |
686	| `refill_ticks` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | int ticks | 0 to the deficit, per `top_up` TAP | Suit D.9 (`cell_deficit_ticks`, `CELL_STOCK_PER_KTICK` [PH]) | the cell credited by one lit bare-hand `top_up` at a home BATTERY port; the stock it withdraws is the home battery's (a store, not a power draw, so invisible to Attention) |
687	
688	**Output Range:** `cell_share_pm` 0 to 1000 (clamped), and 17 to 400 over the realistic and safe-sortie `lit_ticks` above. `sorties_per_cell` is `UNBOUNDED` at `lit_ticks` 0, **56 at the reference line** (28 to 112 across `CELL_S` 600 to 2400), 4 at the 300 s survey and 2 at the 28,800-tick safe-sortie bound. The earlier range "1 to about 56" and the earlier `lit_ticks` bound of 18,000 were wrong at both ends.
689	
690	**Example (FIXTURE-312, the 13-tile pre-ruling schedule; see D.2 fixture convention):** the reference line from arrival to the console with the beam on throughout: `312 + 60 + 240 + 12 + 624 + 30` = 1278 ticks (the 12 is the pickup dwell and the 30 the console approach, both fixture dwells of the D.2 golden schedule) = 21.3 s: `floor(1000 * 1278 / 72000)` = **17 permille** of `CELL_S`, `floor(72000 / 1278)` = 56 sorties. A survey sortie lit for 300 s (18,000 ticks) is **250 permille**: `sorties_per_cell` 4 and `sorties_to_empty` 4. *Built-route reading (indicative, the ruled 28-tile route, D.1):* `672 + 60 + 240 + 12 + 1,344 + 30` = 2,358 lit ticks = 39.3 s, 32 permille, 30 sorties. **Beam left lit across both nominal pod legs** adds 1,884 to 1,896 ticks (2.6 percent of `CELL_S`): the fixture reference line 1,278 becomes 3,162 to 3,174 (`cell_share_pm` 43 to 44, `sorties_per_cell` 22) and a 300 s survey 18,000 becomes 19,884 to 19,896 (276 permille, `sorties_per_cell` 3, `sorties_to_empty` 4). The default expectation is beam off in the pod (Suit AC-SE-36a runs with the beam off); the lit-leg cost is the player's choice *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Each stick thrown aboard adds 180 AU raw (`U_LOUD` [PLACEHOLDER]) to D.2's intake. A 30-minute session of two derelict sorties in the survey style spends about half the cell; the MVP refill is V7 `top_up` at a lit home BATTERY port (user ruling X5, D70b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Campaign reading** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a lit-beam player who surveys at 300 s per sortie empties the cell in about four sorties **between refills**, and then chooses between refilling at home with `top_up`, going dark deliberately, or spending sticks (the authored sticks of the A route, 2 + 2 + 4 = 8, each 150 s, B's shelves not counted). No choice strands them, because the dock console is lit by the pod's status glow whatever the cell (BS-19). The dark-dock strand is therefore no longer a campaign-length event; AC-BS-92 still runs on the campaign-length strand cell, now to prove that the glow holds the invariant. Lighting less (a deliberate dark walk with `toggle_beam`) saves cell and costs sight of the frost sill. *Design-time; the home ship's lamps are fixtures, not the chest lamp.*
691

692	## Edge Cases
693	
694	*Format.* Each case is `If [condition]: [exact outcome]. [rationale]`, ends in its owner's rule-id (Boarding adds no behaviour, BS-1, so an outcome is always an owner's), and carries its id `EC-BS-n` at the end of the bold condition. Cases are grouped by theme; the audit additions of the checkpoint (K15: a DESTROYED node, a store module, a restore in `IN_POD`, the stowed plate, the door that mixes cold) are EC-BS-3, EC-BS-4, EC-BS-40, EC-BS-45 and EC-BS-20, and the dead-bus case (K4) is EC-BS-17. Numbers are design-time and rest on D.1 to D.10. Web Map's constants are registered [PLACEHOLDER] values (see the Format note of Core Rules).
695	
696	### A. Zero, maximum and out of range
697	
698	- **If the player presses `begin_cut` with the welder in hand (`START_EQUIPPED_SLOT` 2) or with no cutter in hand (EC-BS-1)**: the verb answers `NO_TOOL` as an outcome after the press, nothing is cut and no tool-channel tick accrues; `equip_tool` to slot 1 is the fix and its duration is unregistered, so every sortie time stays a lower bound (BS-2 step 1; IA-5, SE-11, SN OQ-SN-6). The wrong tool is an honest, cheap failure, not a hidden gate.
699	- **If the player presses `begin_cap` while carrying, or tries to `equip_tool` the welder with hands full (EC-BS-2)**: both are `BUSY`; the cap is a bare-handed welder act, so the order is cut, cap, then pick up, which follows from "never auto-carried" and not from a rule (BS-8, BS-9; IA-28, SE-11). A second `begin_cap` on an already capped stub is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-26).
700	- **If the node being cut is DESTROYED (EC-BS-3)**: the cut yields `scrap_count` of its repair part and **no module**; there is nothing to carry, the parts are STOWED stock (they ride the body, not the hands), and the cut's noise is spent regardless. A DESTROYED machine is the loudest thing in its room and was never worth a module (IDB-17, LSG:772; K15).
701	- **If the module being cut is a store (the bus battery `b_a2`, the lamp battery `b_a1`) (EC-BS-4)**: its `stock` is discarded into the Graph's `discarded_*` counters so the conservation invariant still closes, and a reinstalled store starts at stock 0 (IDB-18 (i)). A battery has no fluid port, so it leaves no stub; the island re-solves on the next run and what ran on it goes dark, `b_a1` being the stored energy behind A's one residual lamp (DA-27, `[derived]`), so cutting it ends the visible unknown and is a cost the player caused (IDB-18, K15).
702	- **If a second module is wanted while one is carried (EC-BS-5)**: `pickup` answers `BUSY`; the player drops the first in a safe room and shuttles, or leaves it for a second hop, and a second hop costs a second `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] (D.6). The spare `mod_breaker_junction` and `htr_a` cannot ride in the same hop (IA-28, SE-12).
703	- **If a stowed stack cannot take the pickup (a glowstick shelf of 2 with 3 already stowed, or a second `part_hull_plate`) (EC-BS-6)**: the pickup is rejected with Suit's immediate `STACK_FULL`, nothing is taken and nothing is deleted; the stack stays on the shelf and the player throws or uses one first. `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER] 4 and the plate's `stack_max` 1 are the structural bound (IA-28, SE-12, IDB-15).
704	- **If the player holds a tool in the HAND holder when a CARRIED-class yield is picked up (EC-BS-7)**: the pickup is admitted, because "needs hands free" means no carried instance and a held tool is a different holder (SE-12). Recorded as an ask to Interaction to confirm the wording (ASK-BS-I5); until then the sortie tests treat it as admitted (IA-28).
705	
706	### B. The carry-admitted set, doors and drops
707	
708	- **If the console row is refused and the player presses the pod console while carrying (EC-BS-8)**: the press is `BUSY` with no prompt; the module must be dropped first and stays aboard exactly as left, persisting on the dormant derelict, and the carry-home branch is lost. **This state is not shippable for the MVP (BS-9):** it removes the carry home, the loop the MVP exists to test, so the producer treats the refusal as a stop and not a degrade. With a BREACH running it would be the abandon cost, but the failure escalates to the producer as a design blocker and is not an accepted state (BS-9 fallback; C-BS-1; IA-5, WM-24).
709	- **If the carried def is not in the focused hardpoint's `compatible_defs` (EC-BS-9)**: there is no prompt at all, an immediate answer that reads only the carried def and the hardpoint's declaration and never a module-body field, so it is not an oracle (BS-18; MSA-26, IA-11).
710	- **If a FAILED-`hp` instance is installed (EC-BS-10)**: it installs as a FAILED module, `condition_bp` carrying through unchanged, and the home island treats it as dead; no verb refused the install and no reason named the condition, and the consequence is visible in the Graph's channel (a dark lantern, a dry trail, no output) (BS-18; IDB-17, IDB-18, LS-22).
711	- **If a CLOSED door lies on the carry route (the home `door_cargo_s`, or a door the player shut behind them) (EC-BS-11)**: the door face shows its ordinary V4 plate and `set_opening` is Applied (not `BUSY`); the carrier presses it, waits `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` 30 [PLACEHOLDER] and walks through with `carry_ref` unchanged; a door shut as a containment tool is the player's own cost on the way out; during a TELL or BREACH the legal alternative is to abandon the module (BS-10, BS-13; IA-5, IA-24, IA-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
712	- **If every candidate cell for a `drop` is blocked (a threshold square, nine blocked cells) (EC-BS-12)**: `drop` answers immediate `OBSTRUCTED` and the module stays carried; the player steps back a tile and tries again. Door cells answer `NONE` from `floor_tile_at`, so a drop never lands on one, and A and B corridors are 3 wide, so the risk cells are door thresholds only (BS-10; IA-28, DA-7).
713	- **If a SYSTEM-origin close targets a door whose leaf overlaps a carrier's foot box (EC-BS-13)**: the attempt becomes `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries every tick, landing on the first clear tick; the carrier reopens it with the ordinary press (BS-10) at `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` they did not choose. MVP content has no SYSTEM close on a carry route, and a content change that adds one costs a carrier that surprise, which is why it stays an ask (BS-10; IA-24, ASK-BS-I2). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
714	- **If a module is dropped and its section is then welded or cut away before the pickup (EC-BS-14)**: the loose item's position is `(section_id, pos_px)` section-local, so it goes with its section; a section that is cut away takes it with the Graph's `discarded_*` bookkeeping, a loss that belongs to the cut's owner (BS-23; LY-22, LS-16).
715	
716	### C. The cut, the stubs and the faucet
717	
718	- **If the machine being cut is running (the home scrubber, `htr_a` on a woken bus) (EC-BS-15)**: the cut is legal with no special case; the island re-solves on the next run, its dependants go STARVE, and the hum of the thing being cut drops: true-state audio in the consequence channel (LSG:976) that is not in LSG:44's enumerated list, used as true-state corroboration and not the falsifier of record until the Graph rules. The player who cuts their own air has made a P1 choice the world shows at once (BS-7, BS-4; LSG:773, FT:207, C-BS-4).
719	- **If `scr_a` is cut and carried home (EC-BS-16)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: it is a legal cut whose carry ends at a vacant scrubber hardpoint (the committed content route, user ruling D72), where `install_module` is offered by the same plate whether the instance is FAILED or healthy (no oracle, IA-11) and installs it as what it is: a FAILED `scr_a` installs a FAILED module with no take-back (no `remove_module`, MSA-28), in a hardpoint that a healthy module could have filled. That is the stake of the read, and the reference cut stays `htr_a` (BS-17; MSA-26, MSA-28, IDB-14, C-BS-3).
720	- **If `scr_a` is read on A's dead bus (EC-BS-17)**: every lantern is dark, `scr_a`'s and `pump_a`'s alike, and the room's O2 and temperature cannot tell an unpowered healthy scrubber from a FAILED one; the closed-list witnesses falsify "running" and nothing more. A SCAN gives an honest reading (`FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER], scanner in hand), and waking the bus with the spare breaker lights `pump_a`'s lantern while `scr_a`'s stays dark, at the price of the pump-stall clock (90 s) and wear doubled by `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION`. The world told the player it was dead; SCAN or the woken bus tells them it was broken (BS-17; DA-24, DA-25, AC-DA-111, K4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The woken branch buys about 12.9 minutes of unhurried work in the lethal room (DA D.22); the user accepted that modest window as the payoff for waking it (D45), and Derelict Authoring's X-DA-8 reasons log may later trigger one authored payoff that only a served branch delivers. Attention's locus-body pass condition for derelict A is option (b), a fault that wakes when its bus is served (`j_a_main` once fed), confirmed under D47.
721	- **If a stub is never capped, across a restore (EC-BS-18)**: `stubs[]` persists, the hiss persists and nothing forces anything; the leak is a standing consequence-channel truth, bounded by dormancy on a departed derelict (BS-8; IA-26, LS-17, WM-24).
722	- **If two seats target the same node or the same stub (co-op hook) (EC-BS-19)**: the second `begin_cut` is `BUSY` (one job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`), and a second `begin_cap` on a capped stub is `INVALID_TARGET`; the first lit `pickup` of the yield wins and the other seat's is `BUSY` or finds the item gone (BS-7; IA-34, IA-26).
723	- **If the player opens `door_a_spine_machine` and leaves it open (EC-BS-20)**: the "one lethal room" statement is a build-state invariant, so opening the door lets conduction mix the cold into `a_spine` (authored `T0` -12000 mC) for as long as it stays open; the lint prints the open-door projection, the tell stays the frost fan over the sill, and shutting the door behind (a bare-hand V4) is the player's containment act, with its cost on the way out (BS-10; DA-28, DA D.18).
724	- **If a cut node is cut again (EC-BS-21)**: the slot is a SALVAGED tombstone and the verb answers `NOT_SALVAGEABLE`; salvage-once is the faucet's whole shape, and the remaining salvage in a room is read from the empty pedestal rect, the scorched kerf and the stubs, never from a count (BS-16; IDB-17, LSG:243, LY-20, ART 7.4).
725	- **If an abandoned module is revisited on a derelict that went dormant (EC-BS-22)**: the module is in `loose[]` where it was left and the derelict stands as left; if it was dropped in the dark it needs light to re-take, and a dormant room's temperature and gas stand still until the player returns (BS-13, BS-16; LS-17, WM-24, WM-25, WM-28, IA-28).
726	
727	### D. Tells, breach and retreat
728	
729	- **If a tell opens as the cut begins (EC-BS-23)**: the cut completes (240 ticks is well under the played draw), leaving `T - 240` ticks; at the shortest played draw (`TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 [PLACEHOLDER]) a 13-tile carry fits by 36 ticks and a 14-tile carry does not, and at the 600-tick fixture floor 7 tiles is the most; drop-and-run always fits. The cut is loud and forfeits the stillness abort while it runs (BS-7, BS-13; D.3, AT-8, AT-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Under the ruled carry intake the sortie's own tell opens 318 ticks into the carry *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* and not as the cut begins (D.2), so this case is the fixture-armed contract case (`attention_arm_tell`).

### D.7 Traverse bound use (Suit D.11)

The `traverse_bound_use` formula is defined as:

*(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: conformed to Suit's registered vacuum budget, G1/G6; the one-way `RESERVE_S / 2` bound is withdrawn by Suit D.11 and by this GDD)* The lint reads Suit's exported budget (registry `VACUUM_BUDGET_S`, source `suit-and-equipment.md`; Suit D.11, AC-SE-75a, build assertion A15) and does not restate it as a free-standing constant:

`leg_runs = ceil((HOP_LEG_TICKS + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS + IN_POD_SLACK_TICKS) / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` (163 at the defaults) ; `traverse_runs = sum over the path's out and back legs of ceil(tiles_leg x TILE_PX / (V_leg x GRAPH_STEP_TICKS))`, with `V_leg` = `V_WALK` 2 on a leg walked empty and `V_CARRY` 1 on a leg a module is carried ; `TRAVERSE_TOO_LONG iff traverse_runs + 2 x leg_runs > (RESERVE_S - RESERVE_WARN_S) x RUNS_PER_S` (600 at the defaults), written in the cross-multiplied integer form `traverse_runs > VACUUM_BUDGET_RUNS`, where `VACUUM_BUDGET_RUNS = (RESERVE_S - RESERVE_WARN_S) x RUNS_PER_S - 2 x leg_runs` (274; `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 is its seconds form, read from the registry)

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tiles_leg` | int | 0 to 68 | the authored path across the unbreathable compartment(s), per leg | Path length of one leg in tiles (a Manhattan bound, width plus depth, for a room; summed over nested unbreathable rooms on that leg) |
| `V_leg` | int px per tick | `V_WALK` 2 or `V_CARRY` 1 | registry | Speed on that leg: walking empty out, carrying a module back (the lint's reading); a both-ways-carried reading is reported only |
| `TILE_PX` | int px | 48 | registry | Tile size |
| `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, `RUNS_PER_S` | int | 6, 10 | registry; Suit D.8 | Ticks per Graph run; runs per second (`TICK_RATE` / `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) |
| `RESERVE_S`, `RESERVE_WARN_S` | int s | 90, 30 | registry (Suit-owned, `[PLACEHOLDER: Suit]`); SE D.11 | The suit's vacuum or cold reserve and the warn edge the breath clause never reaches |
| `HOP_LEG_TICKS`, `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS`, `IN_POD_SLACK_TICKS` | int ticks | 900, 45, 30 | registry (`HOP_LEG_TICKS`, `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS`); `IN_POD_SLACK_TICKS` is Web Map D.2's derived 30 | The pod leg the reserve also pays for, twice (out and back) |
| `VACUUM_BUDGET_RUNS` | int runs | 274 | derived (Suit D.11); `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 registry | The breath clause's remaining budget for the sortie's unbreathable walking |

**Output Range:** `VACUUM_BUDGET_RUNS` 274 runs (27 s) after two default legs (`2 x 163` = 326 of 600). In tiles: **22 tiles each way when walking out and carrying back** (22 x (4 + 8) = 264, under 274; 23 gives 276 and fails), **34 tiles in total when carried both ways** (34 x 8 = 272; 35 gives 280 and fails), **68 tiles in total walking** (68 x 4 = 272). The former figures (112 walking and 56 carrying, one-way from `RESERVE_S / 2`, and the 56-tile round trip this GDD derived from it) are withdrawn. The lint prints the legs, `traverse_runs`, the budget and the slack in runs.
**Example:** `b_breach` (6 x 5): about 11 tiles each way = 11 x 12 = 132 runs, pass with 142 runs of slack. B's nested worst case (`b_pump` also decompressed, 9 more tiles each way) is 20 tiles each way = 20 x 12 = 240 runs, **34 runs (204 ticks) under 274: PASS only when read by legs** (walk out, carry back). Read as carried both ways (40 tiles = 320 runs) it would fail, so the lint reads legs, and B's nested 40-tile case has only 34 runs of slack; the carry-both-ways reading used by Boarding & Salvage D.4 is a conservative report-only figure and not the gate. A hypothetical 30-tile one-way corridor would fail (30 x 12 = 360 over 274). The warmth clause of Suit D.11 governs a deep-cold room and is checked by D.10 (`COLD_WORK_BUDGET`), not here.

Stride length matches `V_CARRY` (1 px per tick = 60 px/s): **zero foot slip at 60 px/s is an import lint** (ground contact measured per frame); the cycle is re-timed, not the walk cycle slowed. The pack's breath rise (2 to 3 px) continues while carrying; the load signature does not change the silhouette or the walk timing (mass never changes `V_CARRY`, IDB-21). Idle while carrying is the raised hold held still with pack breath only. Pickup and drop transitions are 2 to 3 frames each, no flourish, no ease-in-out beyond a held frame. No exaggeration except Controller- and Suit-driven stagger, recoil and collapse frames; **a carry stagger keeps the module** (PC-8): the module wobbles at most 1 px with the body and is never thrown, dropped or tossed by a stagger frame (a forced drop is a downed event only). Facing is locked during channels (five drawn facings).
1021	
1022	**Cuts, not fades (ART 7.3 spirit).** The module-to-pedestal swap, the loose-sprite appearance, the pickup swap, the cap appearance and the open-end medium ending are all **single-frame cuts**; the optional VS settle on the yield is the only eased motion and has no overshoot. Persistent world motion in a derelict during boarding is limited to dust in the beam, the residual lamp (steady), open-end media (FT) and the player's own breath and steps (ART 2.6, "nothing else moves unless the player moves it"; ART 6.4: nothing decorative moves). **Nothing on or around a salvage node idles, bobs, pulses, glints or sparkles to attract the eye** (G-5, ART 6.4 cap). The HUD bar and prompt follow Interaction's motion list unchanged (no settle, tremor or glide on the bar; the glide is reserved for lying readings, ART 7.3). No HUD element flashes above 3 Hz (HR-13); no full-frame flash on cut completion, hop, breach or pickup.

The cutter and welder sparks obey the 3 Hz ceiling by construction (stepped, stochastic, localized at the grip anchor, never full-frame); the Chemlight pool wanes monotonically and never pulses. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch (user ruling X10, D79), and the flash-counting unit (`ceil(n_transitions / 2)`), `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` weighted per area and the creative-director exemptions are Pixel Pipeline's and the HUD's (user ruling X9), cited and not defined here.

1026	**What a "decide" frame is made of.** Per ART 6.5 ("spend light to read it") the three verdict sentences are distributed across rooms (cause in one, the crew's verb in another, absence in a third); an empty pedestal with a clean kerf is the **absence** sentence for a module the crew themselves cut, and a never-salvaged node is whole. 1167	## Game Feel
1168	
1169	Boarding & Salvage has no input, no frame and no animation of its own (BS-1), so its feel is the feel of **what the composition makes the owners' systems do in sequence**: how long the player is made to stand still before a take, how soon the world answers a cut, how slow and how loud the way home is, and how legal it is to put the prize down. Every number below is either cited from its owner (never restated as ours) or derived from an owner's value by a Formulas entry here. **Units:** 1 tick = 16.7 ms (`TICK_RATE` 60); a tile is `TILE_PX` 48 px; speeds are `V_WALK` 2, `V_RUN` 3 and `V_CARRY` 1 px per tick (24, 16 and 48 ticks per tile). Every sortie duration is a **lower bound** while the tool-swap time is unregistered (`T_EQUIP`, SN OQ-SN-6). Placeholders carry the owner's tag. The target emotion is **a held breath, then a heavy walk**: slow, deliberate, exposed, with one door out that is always open.
1170	
1171	### Feel reference
1172	
1173	**Borrow:** *Project Zomboid*'s carried burden that changes how you move and its timed contextual actions (a linear bar, cancelled by moving, no skill check); the hands-free chest lamp of *Pandorum* (the beam stays on the job while both hands work and while they are full); *Lethal Company*'s run back with hands full and the real story of dropping the scrap to survive; *Alien: Isolation*'s stillness as a strategy. **Anti-reference:** a numeric weight readout or mass-scaled speed (Zomboid's moodle), a repair minigame or quick-time event (a UI surface that could leak module-body truth and a rhythm demand the "I can leave now" test forbids), a motion tracker (an Attention meter in another form, AT-20), and any treasure framing (a pickup glow, a reward chime, a sting).

1196	So the answer to "I started a cut" is a bar and a work pose within one frame, a module that **does not leave its mount for four seconds**, and then, in one frame, a pedestal, a pile and a bang. The answer to "I lifted it" is a changed breath and a prompt that has lost every verb but one. Nothing in this chain is gated on a Boarding tick, because Boarding has none.
1197	
1198	### Weight (the carry is the felt cost)
1199	
1200	- **The ratio is the feel.** Carry : walk : run is **1 : 2 : 3** in px per tick and **3 : 2 : 1** in ticks per tile (48, 24, 16). A 13-tile frame is crossed in 5.2 s walking and 10.4 s carrying. Noise per tile is **24 AU walking, 48 AU carrying, 64 AU running** (`NOISE_PER_TICK` walk 1, carry 1, run 4 [PLACEHOLDER], D.1 and D.2; locomotion only, and a salvage carry aboard the wreck adds 336 AU of burden per tile, D.2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*): carrying is the slowest *and* louder-per-tile than walking, and running is the loudest. Because speed never changes with mass, the 6 kg core and the 90 kg cell feel identical in pace; the difference is the breath (SE-28) and nothing else.
1201	- **No ramp, no slide.** Carry starts and stops instantly like the walk (PCI Game Feel); there is no acceleration curve to read as weight. The weight is the *constant* low speed.
1202	- **Hands full is a verb loss.** On pickup every prompt in the world vanishes except `G . Drop` and, at a fitting hardpoint, the console or a door face, its one press (BS-9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The player feels the carry as a narrowing of what the world offers, not as a number.
1203	- **The pace is the lesson.** A trail, a draught or an alarm sweep that outruns a carrier teaches retreat without text (ART 2.8): at `V_CARRY` the web's propagation is faster than the player; at `V_RUN` after a `drop` it is not.
1204	- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and an animation, never a shove; a carry stagger keeps the module; the walk-only cap at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath (PCI), never a banner.
1205

1212	| Carried sprite to seated machine | one frame | the install is a seat, not a flourish |

1215	| Work loop and sparks stop | the tick the cut completes | no recoil or overshoot (IA recovery 0) |
1216	| Yield settle | none at MVP; VS optional at most 6 ticks, a 4 px drop, no bounce | no eased motion near a salvage node (G-5) |
1217	| Prompt hide | the same render frame the target is lost or unlit | a prompt for an unlit object would lie |
1218	| Rejection | a cut and a dull cue; no shake, flash or red | rejections never decorate (IA V-10) |

1221	### The three rhythms of a sortie
1222	
1223	1. **Boarding rhythm (ART 2.6).** Cold, dead, patient. The player is made to stand still before they are allowed to act: the arrival room offers only the beam, dust, a dried trail and the hull's creaks, and every action after it costs light. Target dwell before the first cut: the player chooses; the design target is that **a player who pauses 2 s or more before the first cut is typical**, not forced (X-BS-2). Nothing moves unless the player moves it.
1224	2. **The tell (ART 2.7).** Beam, ambient, radius, temperature and direction do not change; only the rim of the cone gets busier. The tell is **10 to 30 s** by Pillar 2 and in play **15 to 30 s** (`TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 to `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800 [PLACEHOLDER]); a carry begun at tell entry covers at most 18 tiles (`tell_window_fit`, D.3), so a carry still ahead of more than 18 tiles when the tell opens cannot beat the shortest tell; under the ruled shape the tell opens 318 ticks into a carry of about 21 to 28 tiles, so the *decision* "keep walking with it, or set it down" is live in kind and thin in margin (140 permille of the draw at 28 tiles; the pass line is the boarding spike's, AC-BS-132) (D.2, D.3, **OQ-BS-27**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A cut begun at tell entry completes (240 ticks) and leaves 660 ticks, 13 tiles.
1225	3. **The breach (ART 2.8).** Controlled panic. Alarm Red sweeps for 2 to 3 s, a failure trail runs along a graph edge faster than a carrier walks, and the answer the world teaches is *drop it and go*. `drop` is free; the run at `V_RUN` 3 is three times the carry; the console is one press; the hop is always allowed. There is no forced drop and no refusal (BS-13).

1262	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Pre-ruling history (to the stage-12 revision below, these sentences describe the sortie without the burden term):** Attention's level along this line rises through the sortie. 1264	### Anti-targets (feel the system must not produce)
1265	
1266	A reward chime, sparkle or glow on a take; an inventory or weight readout; a sortie timer; an Attention meter in any channel; a forced drop or a hop refusal; a speed buff, stamina bar or adrenaline state in a tell or breach (rhythm independence: identical input, vitals and load give identical motion in every state); a QTE or minigame in the cut; a stinger on any beat; an autosave toast mid-carry; a hit-stop, shake or flash (Derelict Authoring authors none either).

The spine is a single 3-wide corridor with no side step, so the carrier's exits are the ruled ones and no new one is added: drop the cargo and walk back the way it came (a walker outpaces `V_HUNT_MPX`, HE-24; a horror ahead in the corridor is walked away from, not past, unless it is rooted in REACH, E-HE-25), stand still and go dark if no other light reaches the seat (HE-13), or shut a door behind it (HE-26). **IA-6 Act only on what is lit (`act_gate`).** `act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o)`, where `in_reach` is the Controller's integer predicate (itself including the lit conjunct) and `lit` is Emitter State's hysteresis bit (`LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM`, no dwell). Every PLAYER-origin Interaction command whose declaration is not exempt checks `act_gate` in `validate`, against the exposure table committed at tick T−1 (EM-25). The exceptions are exactly three, plus the actor verbs that are not object verbs: `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an already-lit instrument (PC-6); `throw_glowstick` is an actor verb like `toggle_beam` and needs no lit target (IA-29); and **the self-patch is an actor verb too**: `begin_patch` on object class `ACTOR_SELF` (IA-17) targets the actor's own suit, so there is no object to light and no reach to test; its declaration row has `exempt(row) = 1`, `validate` skips both `in_reach` and `lit` for it, and an ACTOR_SELF row can produce neither `OUT_OF_RANGE` nor `NOT_LIT`. This is not a fourth object exception: the object list stays exactly three (`drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument), and the pod-console refusal below is unchanged. The dark self-patch is still priced, so it is not a free Attention dodge (Pillar 3): TOOL noise on every accrued tick (IA-33), 180 stationary ticks (`PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS`) and the welder in hand. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* **No fourth exception for the pod console (refused, stated here):** Web Map's ASK-I2 and Boarding's ASK-BS-I3 ask that `pod_hop` at the CONSOLE be exempt from the lit condition; the three exceptions are the Controller's PC-6 list (PCI:127) and IA-17 already refuses a fourth, so `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` stay lit-gated (on both the POD_CONSOLE and the DOCK_CONSOLE subject, IA-40), and the hop stays available by content, not by exemption: the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small self-powered status glow that counts as an ordinary lit fixture (not a fourth `act_gate` exception), so `pod_hop`'s lit gate is always satisfied at the console and a `NOT_LIT` at a dock console is a content defect, not a state (Open Question 31, resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2, Web Map option (B); this refusal STANDS.
